webSession.description: Applies to /web/v1 only. The identity is the web sign-in: the OIDC session cookie (`__Host-atrium_session`, or `atrium_session` without HTTPS), a proxy identity from a trusted peer, or the loopback local identity. Every request sends `Atrium-Client: web` (binary content reads may omit it) and no `Authorization` header; `Sec-Fetch-Site`, when sent, is `same-origin`. Unsafe requests also send `X-CSRF-Token` with the `csrf_token` from `GET /web/v1/session` and an `Origin` equal to the host.
webSession.name: __Host-atrium_session

info.description: Prose fields written by the model or the operator, such as message and answer text and the `text` and `thinking` run stream events, are raw markdown: render CommonMark with tables, strikethrough and autolinks, and escape raw HTML. Within v1, responses change only additively: clients ignore unknown error codes, run stream event names and response fields.

put.description: Sets the model, effort and context limit new threads start with. If-Match is optional: send the ETag of GET /assistant/configuration to refuse the change with 412 when the settings changed since it was read; without it the change applies as before.

get.description: The subagent roles the assistant can start, as declared in code: name, description, prompt, effort and tools. Read-only.

The tools the runtime registry holds for the enabled modules: name, the description the model sees, the permission channel that gates each call (by_arguments when the call decides it), the effect class, and the run kinds that may use it. Read-only; the runtime enforces these, the catalog only reports them.

The calendars events can be read from and written to. The id is the calendar path segment of the event routes and the calendar of POST /calendar/events; read_only calendars take no writes. today and timezone are the server's date and zone.

post.description: Creates an event in icloud or google. Each write records an undoable effect; undo it with POST /effects/{id}/undo. Birthdays is read-only.

delete.description: Deletes the event. If-Match is optional: with it, a stale revision gets 412 and nothing is deleted. Undo puts the event back.

get.description: Reads one event live from its provider. The ETag and the revision field carry the event's revision for If-Match.

patch.description: Changes any of title, start, end, all_day, location and notes. If-Match is required: send the revision from the event read; a stale revision gets 412 and nothing is written.

get.description: To do and Waiting in one list: tasks and the commitments from mail the operator owes (`side` todo), and the commitments other people owe the operator (`side` waiting, `owner` them). An item's `ref` is `task:<id>` or `commitment:<id>`, the same id `/queue` uses. Tasks live in the assistant module and commitments in the mail module; the items of a module that is off are left out. Order: todo, then waiting; within each, open, then done, then dismissed; then items with a due date by due date, then items without one; ties by creation time, source and id. `counts` ignore `side`, `status` and the page but apply the other filters. `due_from` and `due_to` are inclusive dates (YYYY-MM-DD) compared with the first ten characters of `due` and leave out items without a due date. `link` is `<kind>:<id>`: tasks match their link, commitments match their `message` or reminder `proposal`. `q` matches a task's title and notes and a commitment's text. `actions` lists the verbs the item accepts; a commitment accepts only status changes. Refetch on an app event `change` for the topic `tasks` (tasks) or `mail` (commitments from mail).

delete.description: Delete a task by `ref`. A commitment from mail accepts only done, dismiss and reopen; edit and delete answer conflict with reason `read_only`. Refetch on an app event `change` for the topic `tasks` (tasks) or `mail` (commitments from mail).

get.description: One To do or Waiting item by `ref`. Refetch on an app event `change` for the topic `tasks` (tasks) or `mail` (commitments from mail).

patch.description: Edit a task by `ref`, as `PATCH /tasks/{task_id}` does. A commitment from mail accepts only done, dismiss and reopen; edit and delete answer conflict with reason `read_only`. Refetch on an app event `change` for the topic `tasks` (tasks) or `mail` (commitments from mail).

post.description: Snooze an open task or commitment by `ref` until `until` (Unix seconds, in the future). The item leaves `/queue` until then and shows `snoozed_until` in `/commitments`. Undoable. Refetch on an app event `change` for the topic `tasks` (tasks) or `mail` (commitments from mail).

put.description: Sets permission rules. If-Match is optional: send the ETag of GET /permissions to refuse the change with 412 when the rules or pending requests changed since it was read; without it the change applies as before.

get.description: The one inbox: everything that waits for the operator, in one order with one count. `total` equals `needs_you` from `GET /shell`, and `total` and `counts` cover the whole queue whatever `kind`, `module`, `cursor` and `limit` are. Order: asks that block the assistant (parked questions, permission requests) first, oldest first; then items with a due time, earliest due first; then everything else, oldest arrival first; ties break on `id`. `module` keeps only the items of that module. Proposal items carry the proposal's `proposal_kind`. Items of a module that is off are left out. An item's `id` is `<source.type>:<source.id>`. Refetch on an app event `change` for any of the topics review, effects, mail, attention, assistant, tasks, calendar, ops, settings and connections; the revision covers the result, so it also moves when an item becomes due or a snooze ends without an event.

One queue item by `id`. `proposal:<proposal_id>` and `draft:<draft_id>` are the items behind `/proposals/{proposal_id}` and `/drafts/{draft_id}`. Not found means the item no longer waits for the operator; read the proposal or draft for its outcome. Refetch on an app event `change` for any of the topics review, effects, mail, attention, assistant, tasks, calendar, ops, settings and connections; the revision covers the result, so it also moves when an item becomes due or a snooze ends without an event.

The next 5 times a cadence would run in the server zone, parsed and stepped by the scheduler's own code. A cadence it cannot parse is 422 invalid with the reason on the schedule field, as when creating a schedule.

patch.description: Changes any of schedule, prompt, name and enabled. If-Match is optional: send the schedule's revision to refuse the change with 412 when it changed since it was read; without it the change applies as before.

post.description: Asks the running serve to run the schedule now, through the same pause, module and budget checks as a scheduled run, and answers at once with the requested run: run is its id. Its thread_id is set once serve starts it; read it from GET /schedules/{job_id}/runs/{run_id}.

get.description: One run of a schedule, the same row as in GET /schedules/{job_id}/runs. thread_id stays null until serve starts the run.

get.description: The task list of the Plan and Tasks pages. Order: open, then done, then dismissed; within each, tasks with a due date by due date, then tasks without one; ties by creation time and id. `counts` ignore `status` and the page but apply the other filters. `due_from` and `due_to` are inclusive dates (YYYY-MM-DD) compared with the first ten characters of `due` and leave out tasks without a due date. `link` is `<kind>:<id>` and keeps the tasks linked to that subject. `q` matches title and notes. Refetch on the `tasks` topic.
